candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Health Promotion and Maintenance, printed p.9 / PDF p.13
candidate.educational_objective: Teach parents the established pediatric health risks of secondhand smoke.

options.A: Secondhand smoke can cause respiratory infections, ear disease, asthma attacks, and sudden infant death syndrome in infants and children.
options.B: Secondhand smoke is safe if exposure lasts less than one hour.
options.C: Opening a window completely eliminates a child’s exposure to secondhand smoke.
options.D: Secondhand smoke affects adults but has no established effects in children.

candidate.rationale: CDC states there is no safe level of secondhand smoke exposure. In infants and children it causes or increases risk for respiratory infections, middle ear disease, asthma attacks, and sudden infant death syndrome. Ventilation or opening a window does not eliminate exposure.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Secondhand smoke causes important pediatric respiratory and ear disease and SIDS; no safe exposure level is known.
candidate.source_document_title: Health Problems Caused by Secondhand Smoke
candidate.source_locator: Overview / pediatric effects—SIDS, respiratory infections, ear infections, asthma attacks; no safe exposure level
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
candidate.stem: Which statement should the nurse include when teaching parents about secondhand smoke exposure?
